chapter_theme: One song at Kottaiyur (கொட்டையூர்): the poet, called wicked, troublesome, mad and fallen for his surrender to women, asks for the golden lotus feet and a place among the purified devotees; the praise tells of Sita's abduction and Ravana's ten heads cut.

871.reading: The poet tells how, falling into the hands of parrot-like women whose silk bodices loosen over pearl strings, he melted under their sway and by ruined deeds wanders called wicked, troublesome, mad, fallen and cruel-minded, and asks Murugan to cut his sorrow, set his golden lotus feet on him and place him among the devotees of the purified state. The praise tells how Ravana carried the golden creeper of the lotus off in his chariot to a grove in the far south and imprisoned her, and how the victor cut his ten crowned heads and many arms, ending his pride, and names the lord of Kottaiyur whom the victorious worship.
871.nuance: துட்டனெனக் கட்டனெனப் பித்தனெனப் ப்ரட்டனென: the names are what others call him, a public shame. The praise piles up அற ('cut off, ended') through the line on Ravana, a sound-play. பதவிச் சுத்தி அணைப் பத்தர் is hard to divide.
